column2: How do I play “The right date”?
column3: Open the Game, choose “📅 The right date”. You get a family event (birth, marriage, death… and, if you like, major dates in French history) without its date: drag it onto “⬇ Here” at its place on the timeline, or choose the place with the keyboard (Tab then Enter). Right: the card stays and you score a point; wrong: it moves to its real place and you lose a life. Set the number of cards, the minimum gap between two dates (the bigger it is, the easier) and the lives. “About” dates are marked “≈”; two dates that cannot be told apart go either way.

column2: How do I play noughts and crosses with my own rules?
column3: Open the Game, choose “❌ Free-rules noughts and crosses”. Choose the grid (from 3×3 to 30×30), how many in a row to win (3, 4, 5…), whether diagonals count, gravity (the pieces drop, as in “Connect 4”) or a grid that grows when you play at the edge. From 2 to 6 players, each with their symbol (❌ ⭕ ⭐ 🌳 ♥…, a letter or an ancestor’s portrait) and their colour; a player can be the computer (simple or medium). “↻ Play again” starts a new round keeping the evening’s scores; “↶ Undo the last move” to make up for a mistake. Ready-made sets: Classic noughts and crosses, Connect 4, Five in a row, Endless grid. “🧮 Play until the grid is full” option: you don’t stop at the first line, each line scores a point (a line twice as long is worth two), and the most points wins.

column2: How do I make a jigsaw puzzle with a family photo?
column3: Open the Game (games table in the archive room), choose “🧩 Jigsaw” in “Game”. Take the image from your database (“🖼 Choose from the database”), a person’s record photo (“👤 A person’s photo”), or drag an image from the computer: it goes into the media. Choose the number of pieces (12 to 1000, or “Other…”), the shape (real pieces or squares), rotated pieces if you like (right-click or R to turn them), then “Start”. The pieces snap into the right place and against their neighbour; wheel or pinch to zoom, ⛶ for full screen. The timer runs while you play: Space or ❚❚ to pause (the image blurs); it also stops when you switch tabs. The game is stored in your genealogy database: it saves itself (a few seconds after your last move, on pause and when you leave the screen), “✓ Saved” shows it in the bar, and “💾 Save” (⌘S) does it straight away. Click the name at the top to change it. You find it again in the left column, even on another computer or after restoring a backup, exactly where you were (pieces, groups, time). If the app stops responding, the game is kept in the browser and goes into the database as soon as possible. At the end: your time, your record for this image and this number of pieces, and the history of finished puzzles.

column2: How do I play patience (solitaire card games)?
column3: Open the Game, choose “🂠 Patience (card games)” in “Game”, then the game among 131 patiences arranged by family (Klondike, FreeCell, Spider, Yukon, Forty Thieves, Castles and gardens, pairing games). Drag a card (or a sequence) onto another pile, or click it then click where to put it; double-click: onto a foundation; click on the stock: draw. In pairing games (Pyramid, Elevens, Thirteens…), click the cards that go together.

Twenty-three more, with their rules in the game’s “📖 The rules”: Agnes Sorel, White Horse, Four Seasons, Chameleon, Double Canfield, ForeCell, Fan with cells, Mrs Mop, Black Widow, Three Blind Mice, Gypsy, Irmgard, Queenie, Brisbane, Blockade, Good Fortune, Cadet, Martha, Morehead, Montana (the gaps: you arrange each row from 2 to King by sliding cards into the gaps, “🔀 Redeal” twice), Nestor (pairs of the same value), Pairs and All in a row.

column2: How do I play cards against the computer (Belote, Tarot, Hearts…)?
column3: Open the Game, choose “🂡 Multiplayer card games” in “Game”, then the game: War, Crazy Eights, Hearts, President, Belote (with 4, you and North against West and East, with declarations), 4-player Tarot (bid, guard, kitty, Excuse, Petit au bout), Rummy (gin, for two) or Crapette (for two). The number of players follows the game; you are the only person at the table, the others are the computer 🤖, each at their level (easy, medium or hard). The rules are in the “?” of the game bar. Click a card in your hand to play it (with the keyboard: ← → then Enter); ↶ undoes your last move (⌘Z), 💡 gives a tip, Esc pauses.

column2: Card games: can the Kings, Queens and Jacks have my ancestors’ faces?
column3: Yes: in “New game”, leave “🖼 Kings, Queens and Jacks with my ancestors’ portraits” and choose the people (your Sosa ancestors, a generation, a branch or the whole genealogy). The Kings and (in Tarot) the Knights are men from the oldest generations, the Queens women, the Jacks younger men; their photo is taken from their record. Never a living person or a confidential record. “🤖 The computer bears ancestors’ names” also gives their names to the computer players.

column2: Patience: how do I undo a move or get help?
column3: “↶ Undo” (or Ctrl+Z / ⌘Z) undoes moves without limit during the game. “💡 A possible move” shows in yellow a card to play and where to put it. “⬆ Move all up” sends to the foundations everything that can go there; “⟲ Same deal” replays the same cards from the start. Each game keeps your record (time and moves).

column2: ☢ The bunker: where can I see my achievements and my best games?
column3: The bunker is hidden in the archive room (photo lab, three clicks on the red lamp). On its home screen, or in the game (⋯ at the top, and at the end of a game): “🏆 Achievements and records”. About thirty achievements (hold out 30 days, ten inhabitants, no deaths, build everything, a winter without a stove, a birth, fend off 3 raids, all the plans found, ten items made, one per scenario won…), some hidden (“?”) until you earn them. Each achievement earned is announced at the bottom left and keeps its date; a table shows the best games (days held, inhabitants, scenario, difficulty). Everything stays on this computer, never in the database.

column2: ☢ The bunker: how do I play with my ancestors in 1709, 1720, 1870, 1910 or 1940?
column3: In “New game”, choose a scenario from “📜 In history, with your ancestors”: the great winter of 1709 (extreme cold), the plague of Marseille in 1720 (epidemic), the siege of Paris in 1870 (rationing, shells), the great Paris flood of 1910 (flooding), the exodus of 1940 (refugees, scarce petrol). The line below says how many ancestors of your family were alive at that date (born before, died after): they go down into the shelter, those from the region first; if some are missing, invented inhabitants of the period complete the group, and the game says so. Never a living person or a confidential record. The setting follows the period: no electricity in 1709, 1720 and 1870 (candle, fireplace, workshop by hand), the town crier and the gazette instead of the radio, period odds and ends and plans.

column2: ☢ The bunker: can I go back after a mistake?
column3: Yes: every morning at 6 a.m., the game is saved (the last 7 mornings). “⋯ → ⏪ Resume on the morning of day…” (or the button at the end of a lost game) shows the list of mornings with the inhabitants and the supplies; “Resume that morning” asks nothing, and “↶ Undo” in the message at the bottom left brings you back to where you were. An achievement rewards those who hold out 30 days without ever going back.

column2: ☢ The bunker: where do I find the plans for new items?
column3: By searching the town. Each plan comes mostly from certain places (the beehive and the cider press at the farm, the accordion at the church, the fish traps at the harbour, the compass at the library…); the 🛠️ Workshop tab → “❔ To find” says so for each one; “rare” plans are found much less often. About twenty extra items, each with a real effect: well (water without rain), smokehouse, beehive, press, fish traps (food), eiderdowns (less cold), lanterns, clock, accordion, chess, wine cellar (morale), herb garden, grandmother’s medicine chest, stretcher (health), gutters, trap pit, arrow slits, compass, sledge, washtub, dovecote (news without electricity), solar oven and small turbine (not in the old-time scenarios). The places sometimes turn up a notebook of plans in the morning.

column2: ☢ The bunker: how do I send an expedition into the region?
column3: “🗺️ Region” tab: the map of the surroundings, drawn by the game (other towns — often those in your tree —, villages, farms, abbeys, depots, forests, mines, harbour), linked by roads that are more or less long and dangerous (green safe, yellow, orange, red very dangerous; dashed along the water). Click a known place, then “🧭 Form a convoy…”: who goes, to do what (search, trade, help, attack), which way (the shortest or the safest), the transport, the tools taken and the provisions (“＋ Plan just enough for the road”). The convoy leaves for several days: those who have left do not work at the bunker. You follow the convoy on the map and on the radio (or through the town crier): ambushes, accidents, finds, someone who joins you… It comes back with what it found, plans, wounded, news, new inhabitants, a pack animal — or not at all. “📻 Come back!” makes it turn around.

column2: ☢ The bunker: who are the other groups of survivors?
column3: In the “🗺️ Region” tab, at the bottom: friendly neighbours, traders and rival gangs, each settled somewhere on the map, with a reputation from −100 to +100 (Enemies, Wary, Neutral, Friendly, Allies). It rises when you share, trade honestly, give (🎁 Give…) or come to help them, and falls when you refuse a request for help, rob a trader (“🦹 Steal” button at the hatch: everyone ends up knowing) or attack them. What it changes: better deals with those who like you, help from your allies when things go badly, and gangs who hold a grudge attack more often and harder (paying them what they ask calms them for two days). The groups also sometimes ask for help: “🤲 Share” or “Refuse”.

column2: ☢ The bunker: what are the ruined buildings in the town for?
column3: On the town plan (“🏙️ Town” tab): a farm, a well, a mill, an infirmary, a forge… (with the period name). “🔨 Start the building work” takes the materials, then you have to send inhabitants to work there (“👷 Work 8 h”) until the work is finished. Then the building produces something every day (food, water, medicines, parts…), kept on site for up to three days: go and collect it (“🧺 Go and collect”). A building that is not visited can be looted or damaged (it then has to be repaired); a palisade protects it better.

column2: ☢ The bunker: how does an inhabitant learn a trade?
column3: In the “👥 Inhabitants” tab, an expert inhabitant (their trade, or ×1.4 in a skill) or an elderly one (60 and over) has the “🎓 Train an apprentice…” button: choose the skill and the apprentice. Each evening when both are at the bunker, the apprentice progresses (never beyond their master); the log reports it week by week. When the master dies, their knowledge stays with the apprentice (and after two weeks, their notebooks help catch up to their level).
